audit.whatIsWrong: content win[] gives Urgot all seven stages, but whys[4] says Level 6 is even, whys[5] says first item tips sustained brawls to Aatrox, and whys[6] says the itemised drain out-lasts him in the 1v1. The prose in mid and late says the same. The packet chart reads Urgot through Levels 4-5, Skill at Level 6, then Aatrox.
audit.why: Purge locks Urgot in place and slows him while it runs, so once Aatrox's kit and first item exist he wins any fight Urgot commits Purge into. 50.16% over 1850 games is a lane that ends even, not one Urgot owns start to finish.
audit.corrected: Level 6 evens to Skill; First item and Two+ items read Aatrox.

audit.whatIsWrong: Fear Beyond Death is called 'a low-cooldown execute' in late with no number, and the spikes tell you to play around a timer they never give.
audit.why: Fear Beyond Death is 100/85/70 — that is not low, it is the longest cooldown in the matchup and the single most trackable timer you have. Corrosive Charge is 10s at rank 1 and Disdain 16s.
audit.corrected: 100s rank-1 R, 10s Q and 16s Disdain written into the spikes, mid and late.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry says 'walk in during his Purge lockout' without ever explaining what the lockout is, and it never states the targeting rule that makes Urgot's damage land. Purge slows Urgot himself while it runs, and it PRIORITISES champions he has recently struck with another ability — so eating a Corrosive Charge is what marks you for the shotgun. Disdain is also mis-described as a 'shield-shotgun trade': it is a charge that shields him and hurls the champion he catches out of his way.
audit.why: Riot's text: Purge — 'Urgot slows himself while he unloads his weapon on nearby enemies. Prioritizes enemy champions Urgot has recently struck with other abilities'; Disdain — 'Urgot charges in a direction, shielding himself and trampling non-champion enemies. If he catches an enemy champion, he will stop and hurl them out of his way.' Dodging the 10s Corrosive Charge is not just about the slow — it is what stops Purge from tracking you at all. And Disdain is a displacement, so it is what ends your combo, not a damage tool.
audit.corrected: Purge's self-slow and its ability-mark priority stated in spikes[0] and mid; Disdain named as a shielded charge that flips you out of the fight.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Walk in during his Purge lockout' is the right instruction attached to the wrong cooldown, because Purge reaches 0s at rank 5.
audit.why: Purge is 12/9/6/3/0 — by the time he maxes it there is no cooldown window to wait for at all. The window is the duration he is locked slowing himself, not a cooldown, and the only real cooldowns to count are Corrosive Charge (10s) and Disdain (16s).
audit.corrected: Windows re-anchored onto the 10s Q and 16s Disdain, with Purge described as a commitment rather than a cooldown.

edits.before: The lane finally evens here: dodge his Corrosive Charge (Q) shells, walk in during his Purge (W) lockout, and land the third-Q knockup to stop him kiting with legs.
edits.after: The lane evens here: dodge Corrosive Charge (10s) — Purge hunts whoever he last hit with an ability — and walk in while Purge slows him in place. Then land the third-Q knockup.

edits.before: World Ender lets you brawl through his shield-shotgun trades and tips the fight your way, but respect his R (Fear Beyond Death) execute — don't dive in low or he'll flip and finish you.
edits.after: World Ender brawls through his legs, but respect Fear Beyond Death (100s): below its threshold he executes. Disdain (16s) shields him and hurls you out of the fight — never commit into both.

edits.before: From level 4-5 the lane evens out and your first item tips it to Aatrox — your Q sweetspots and drain beat his sustained shotgun trades if you catch him mid-Purge. The key is his W lockout: when he commits Purge he can't reposition, so that's your window to E in, pull with W, and land the knockup. Just track his R at 6 — Fear Beyond Death executes, so never trade down into a flip.
edits.after: From level 4-5 the lane evens and your first item tips it to Aatrox — your Q sweetspots beat his legs if you catch him mid-Purge. Purge slows Urgot himself while it runs, so his commit is your window: dash in, chain, knockup. Dodging the 10s Corrosive Charge matters twice over, since Purge prioritises whoever he last hit with an ability. Track the 100s Fear Beyond Death and never trade down into it.

edits.before: Urgot builds tanky and keeps a low-cooldown execute plus strong zoning legs, but once you're itemised your drain out-lasts his shotgun DPS in a straight 1v1. The one thing to fear is his R flip execute — play around its timer, all-in when it's down, and use your teamfight R heal amp rather than trading into a low-HP flip.
edits.after: Urgot builds tanky and zones with his legs, but once you are itemised your drain out-lasts his shotgun DPS in a straight 1v1. The one thing to fear is Fear Beyond Death — on 100s at rank 1 it is trackable, so all-in the moment it is spent and never fight below its execute threshold with it up.

edits.before: Kite backward with W active while his passive legs proc
edits.after: Mark you with a Q shell so Purge locks on to you first

edits.before: Urgot changes the lane by forcing Aatrox to respect Urgot E and R execute. Aatrox wins by controlling spacing with his first two Q swings, holding E until the enemy punish tool is committed, and managing the wave so the enemy must walk into the outer edge of his Q. Urgot wants to force long trades, punish overextension, and turn one bad Aatrox cooldown into a lane-losing fight.
edits.after: Urgot changes the lane by forcing Aatrox to respect Disdain (E, 16s), a shielded charge that hurls him out of his own combo, and a 100s Fear Beyond Death that executes him outright. Aatrox wins by dodging the 10s Corrosive Charge, because Purge hunts whoever Urgot last struck with an ability, and by walking in during the seconds Purge slows Urgot in place.
